A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
A. fumigatus attaches to alveolar macro phages by a mechanism that involves a mannose/fucose receptor and a receptor that recognizes chitin.
A. fumigatus binds to murine pulmonary alvolar macrophages by two mechanisms, one mediated by a mannosyl-fucose lectin and the second by a chitin-specific lectin.
A. fumigatus binds to the murine macrophage via two different lectin-like sites, one that recognizes mannosylfucose and another that recognizes chitin.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the lectin-like sites are present on alveolar macrophaes and that they are involved in the attachment of conidia to alveolar macrophas.
the mannosyl fucosyl receptor is a key mediator of conidial attachment to alveolar macropahages.
A. fumigatus binds to the murine alveolar macrophiage via two distinct mechanisms.
